summary: Makes a panel drag-to-move, with optional axis locking and a limit on how far it may travel.
overview: Drop it on a panel, or on a title-bar child, to make it movable — repositionable HUD elements, floating debug windows, pull-out drawers.

Three restrictions can apply, and they COMBINE rather than override one another: an axis lock, a limit on distance from the panel's home position, and a clamp to the parent's bounds. Whichever is tightest at any moment is the one you feel.
useCases: A debug or inspector window the developer can move.
HUD elements the player can reposition.
A drawer or tray that pulls out only so far, then stops.
A slider-like handle constrained to one axis.

params.tuning: Defaults to this object's own RectTransform. Set it to the panel root when the component lives on a title bar.

params.why: Which directions the panel may travel in.
params.tuning: A locked axis receives no movement at all — the delta is zeroed before it is applied, so the panel cannot drift even a pixel. Vertical is what turns this into a drawer; Horizontal suits a handle or a slide-out tray.

params.why: Keeps the panel fully inside its parent's bounds.
params.tuning: Off, a panel can be dragged completely off screen and become unreachable. Works for any anchor and pivot — see the gotcha below if you knew this to be broken before.

params.why: Limits how far the panel may travel from its HOME position.
params.tuning: Home is captured once, when the component wakes — not per drag. That distinction is the whole feature: measured per drag, you could pull 200px, release, pull 200px again, and the limit would cap nothing. Call SetHomeToCurrentPosition if your own code moves the panel afterwards.

params.why: Furthest LEFT and DOWN from home, in pixels. Negative values.
params.tuning: Use 0 on an axis to forbid movement that way entirely — a drawer that pulls down but never rises above its rest is minOffset (0, -260), maxOffset (0, 0). Written the wrong way round, min and max are ordered rather than obeyed literally, because the alternative is a silent teleport.

params.why: Furthest RIGHT and UP from home, in pixels. Positive values.
params.tuning: Same rules as minOffset. Both are ignored entirely while Limit Range is off.

apiNotes.HomePosition: The anchoredPosition the range is measured from, captured when the component woke.
apiNotes.SetHomeToCurrentPosition(): Re-bases the range on wherever the panel is now. Needed if your code or a layout group repositions the panel after Awake, or the range still refers to a place it no longer occupies.
apiNotes.FilterDelta(Vector2, DragAxis): Pure and static — the axis rule on its own. Public so it is testable without a live EventSystem and reusable by anything that moves the panel itself.
apiNotes.ClampToConstraints(Vector2): Takes a desired anchoredPosition and returns the allowed one, with every enabled restriction applied. This is the whole constraint system as one callable function, which is what lets the self-test exercise it against real RectTransforms with no canvas and no input.

gotchas.title: Clamp To Parent was wrong for anything but a centre-anchored panel — fixed
gotchas.body: It used to assume anchoredPosition was measured from the parent's CENTRE. It is actually measured from the anchor, so a panel anchored anywhere else was clamped to a window offset by the gap between the two. The toolkit's own UIPolish demo anchors at (0.75, 0.75) on a 1280-wide canvas and could be dragged roughly 320px off the right edge with this switched on. It now derives the panel's centre by transforming a real point instead of reconstructing it from anchor maths, which is correct for any anchor, any pivot and a stretched rect alike.

gotchas.title: The restrictions intersect — they are not applied in order
gotchas.body: Each enabled restriction narrows one allowed window, and the panel is clamped into it once. Applying them one after another would be order-dependent: clamping to the range and then to the parent lets the parent step push the panel back outside the range. If a drag stops sooner than you expect with both on, the other restriction is the tighter one.

gotchas.title: Dragging fights a layout group
gotchas.body: A panel under a layout group has its position overwritten every rebuild. Drag panels that are not laid out — and if a layout does position it once at startup, call SetHomeToCurrentPosition afterwards so the range is measured from where it actually landed.

gotchas.title: A panel larger than its parent pins to an edge
gotchas.body: With Clamp To Parent on, an oversized panel produces a genuinely inverted allowed window. The bounds are ordered rather than trusted, so it settles against an edge instead of jumping or producing NaN — but the real fix is not to clamp a panel bigger than the thing containing it.
